title: Chapter 6.  Polity & Governance — Current Structure & Leadership

blocks.content: This chapter covers Puducherry's present-day governmental structure and current officeholders, including the results of the April 2026 Assembly election — the most recent and highest-value current-affairs material for this UT.

cells: Shri K. (Kuniyil) Kailashnathan, a retired IAS officer (1979 batch, Gujarat cadre), in office since 7 August 2024
Shri N. Rangasamy (All India N.R. Congress, AINRC), sworn in for a FIFTH term on 13 May 2026, following the NDA's victory in the April 2026 Assembly election
Held 9 April 2026 (single phase, all 30 seats); results declared 4 May 2026; record turnout of approximately 90% — the highest ever for a Puducherry Assembly election

NDA alliance (AINRC + BJP + AIADMK + LJK) won 18 of 30 seats, an increased majority compared to 2021 — AINRC 12, BJP 4, AIADMK 1, LJK 1; opposition Secular Progressive Alliance (Congress + DMK + allies) won the remaining seats, including a poor showing for the Indian National Congress
A. Namassivayam (BJP) held the Home portfolio in the previous term; specific 2026 cabinet portfolio allocations were finalised shortly after the government's formation

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: N. Rangasamy's May 2026 swearing-in was his FIFTH term as Chief Minister of Puducherry — a notable personal and political milestone, reflecting his position as by far the most dominant individual political figure in Puducherry's post-Independence history (see also Chapter 12).

cells: 1 (unreserved, covering the entire UT); current MP (since 2024): V. Vaithilingam (INC)
Madras High Court (Puducherry has no dedicated High Court of its own)
Municipalities/Commune Panchayats in each of the four regions, functioning under Puducherry-specific local-body regulations

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Puducherry's judiciary falls under the Madras High Court — a frequently tested fact given the UT's otherwise distinct (non-Tamil-Nadu) constitutional and administrative identity; Puducherry does NOT have its own dedicated High Court, unlike Delhi (which does).

items: Current LG (2026): K. Kailashnathan, since 7 August 2024.
Current CM (2026): N. Rangasamy (AINRC), sworn in for his 5th term on 13 May 2026, after the NDA's April 2026 Assembly election win.
2026 Assembly election: NDA (AINRC+BJP+AIADMK+LJK) won 18/30 seats; record ~90% voter turnout.
1 Lok Sabha seat (current MP: V. Vaithilingam, INC, since 2024); 1 Rajya Sabha seat.
Judiciary under the Madras High Court — Puducherry has no dedicated High Court of its own.
